inputs.base_revenue_note: LTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 4,951.1 - 9M-2025 3,677.2 + 9M-2026 3,906.7. LTM is used as FY0 so the revenue base, the Sep-2026 balance sheet and the Sep-2026 share count all sit on the same date; Y1 is the twelve months to Sep-2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 Sep 2026: 122.328M Class A outstanding (10-Q cover/balance sheet) + 0.617M in-the-money RSU/option/ESPP dilution (Q3 diluted 125.696M less basic 125.079M) + 0.941M antidilutive RSUs/PSUs included for conservatism. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; Q4-2026 repurchases (~$450M/qtr pace) are NOT credited.
inputs.total_debt_note: Carrying value at 30 Sep 2026 (14.9 current + 3,756.4 non-current). Face value is 3,810.7 (2029 TL 1,433.2; 2031 TL 977.5; 2027 notes 600.0; 2029 notes 800.0).
inputs.sbc_ltm_note: FY2025 figures above are the last full-year base for the owner-FCF history. LTM to Sep-2026: reported FCF 1,743.8 (OCF 1,772.3 - capex 28.5), SBC 289.6 (5.6% of revenue), owner FCF 1,454.2 before the ~$140M/yr of cash interest the reported figure already bears. Q3-2026 SBC alone was 5.0% of revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: GoDaddy is a net-debt company (interest income ~$37M FY2025 against ~$150M interest expense), so interest income is not stripped from the FCF base. The component build is unlevered (EBITDA -> tax -> capex), so neither interest expense nor interest income enters the projected flows; net debt is deducted once in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement add-back ($317.8M) == NEBITDA reconciliation line 'Equity-based compensation expense' ($317.8M). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed in financing activities, so no equity-award tax is added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $1,601.9M; 9M-2026 $1,305.0M under the $3.0B authorization running to end-2027. Shares fell from 134.7M (Dec-2025) to 122.3M (Sep-2026). The flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention: buybacks run at ~5x the SBC charge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.1 = cost of equity ~9.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (blended effective rates 3.7-6.1% on the 10-Q debt table), after-tax ~4.5%; market-weight debt ~21% of capital => WACC ~8.6%. Rounded UP to 9.0% for the live structural-disruption debate and ~1.5x net debt/EBITDA. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not again through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases (liabilities ~$91M, lease cash ~$35M/yr) are expensed inside EBITDA as opex; no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path = 0) and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest since 2023 (NCI income nil FY2024-FY2025); attributable = consolidated.
inputs.tax_note: Cash taxes paid were $16.5M FY2025 and $19.3M 9M-2026 against a GAAP provision of $145.0M and $215.0M, because US federal/state DTAs ($845.7M at Sep-2026, down from $1,052.6M at Dec-2025) shelter US income. At ~$200M/yr of deferred-tax consumption the shelter lasts roughly four more years, so the cash tax rate ramps 3% -> 23% over Y1-Y5 and is NOT perpetuated. 23% = 21% federal + state + foreign mix.
inputs.working_capital_note: Deferred revenue grows with bookings (bookings 5,400 vs revenue 4,951 in FY2025) and is a real cash inflow: net operating WC inflow was 130.5 (FY2023), 61.2 (FY2024), 103.0 (FY2025) against revenue increases of 162.8, 319.1, 377.9 => 34% average capture, 88% in 9M-2026 on payables timing. Base captures 25% of the revenue CHANGE, so the tailwind fades as growth decelerates.
inputs.da_capex_note: D&A has fallen from 199.6 (FY2021) to 77.0 LTM (1.5% of revenue) as acquisition intangibles roll off; capex is 0.55% of revenue LTM (28.5) plus a one-off $17.5M ICANN registry-rights application fee. D&A glides to 1.0% and capex rises to 0.8% so the two converge; D&A above capex only matters through the tax shield.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating company, consumer internet / SaaS-like SMB platform). Fresh build - no prior DCF or memory entry. House basis expenses SBC fully and holds the count flat. EBITDA margin anchors to NEBITDA (33.4% LTM, guided >33% FY2026) less ~0.4pp of recurring 'restructuring and other' that NEBITDA excludes. Reported FCF is levered (after ~$140M cash interest), so the unlevered year-1 component build (~27-28% owner-FCF margin) sits slightly below the LTM unlevered equivalent (~30%) because WC capture is normalised to 25% from the 88% 9M-2026 print. Market context at the price: EV/NEBITDA ~9.7x, EV/company-FCF ~9.6x - the 2026 AI-disintermediation de-rating (52w 71.59-133.34) is the valuation question, and it is carried in the bear weight, not the WACC.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 revenue guidance (~6%, $5.215-5.255B, upper end) corroborated by the 3yr revenue CAGR of 6.6%; equity CAGR is unusable (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity is near zero or negative (215.1 at Dec-2025, -138.8 at Sep-2026) after $6.7B of buybacks since 2019, so the equity CAGR the method prefers is undefined. EPS CAGRs are also omitted: FY2023 EPS ($9.08 diluted) embeds a $971.8M valuation-allowance release and FY2024 a $171.5M tax benefit, so EPS growth measures tax accounting, not the business. Revenue (6.6%/8.3%) and owner FCF (24.2%/19.9%) are the usable series; owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported-FCF CAGR because SBC grew 3.7%/yr over FY2022-25 while FCF grew ~20%/yr, i.e. SBC is a FALLING share of cash flow (6.5% -> 6.4% -> 5.6% LTM of revenue).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped, net-debt company). The 20%+ FCF CAGR is margin expansion and near-zero cash tax, not revenue; it will not persist once the DTA shelter is consumed, which is why the forward cash tax rate ramps to 23%.

base.narrative: Guidance-anchored: Y1 at the ~6% FY2026 guide (Core ~4%, A&C ~10%), decelerating to 2.5% as the Core Platform matures and Airo roughly offsets legacy website-builder migration. NEBITDA margin expands ~50bp/yr to 35% (management delivered ~100bp/yr FY2023-26 and guides >33%). SBC glides 5.5% -> 4.0%. Cash tax ramps to 23% as DTAs are consumed. 16x terminal cap for a low-single-digit grower; Gordon at 9%/2.5% (~15.8x) binds.

bull.narrative: Airo converts: its >$100M annualised bookings run-rate (from ~$10M in Q1-2026) keeps compounding and lifts A&C to mid-teens growth, Core holds ~4-5% on ARPU and the new gTLD round, and total growth re-accelerates to 8% in Y2-Y3 before fading to 3%. Scale on a fixed cost base and the completed infrastructure consolidation take NEBITDA to 37%. Bookings growth lifts deferred-revenue capture to 30%. Same WACC and tax path as base; the bull is a growth-and-margin case, not a cheaper-capital case.

bear.narrative: AI disintermediation bites: AI-native presence tools and closed platforms shrink the need for a dedicated domain and templated site, Core growth fades to zero by Y5 as customer count (flat at ~20.5M since 2021) starts to erode, Airo only cannibalises legacy website products rather than adding net bookings, and price competition from Wix/Squarespace/Cloudflare/Namecheap plus AI compute spend compress NEBITDA to 31%. SBC stays at 5% to retain engineering talent. Deferred-revenue capture falls to 15% with bookings. 1% terminal growth and a 12x cap: a melting-ice-cube exit multiple. Cash tax still normalises - the DTA shelter is not a bear-case asset.

scenario_narratives.base: GoDaddy stays the default identity-and-presence layer for ~20.5M SMBs: ~6% growth in FY2026 fading to 2.5% as Core Platform matures and Airo offsets legacy website-builder migration; NEBITDA margin rises ~50bp/yr to 35%; SBC glides from 5.5% to 4% of revenue; the DTA tax shelter is consumed by ~2030 and cash tax normalises at 23%; buybacks keep the count flat and are value-neutral in the house model.
scenario_narratives.bull: Airo scales from a >$100M run-rate into a genuine growth engine, A&C re-accelerates to mid-teens, ANS gives GoDaddy an identity role in the agentic internet, total growth re-accelerates to 8% before fading, and NEBITDA reaches 37% on a fixed-cost base. Value is a growth-and-margin outcome at the same 9% WACC.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 AI-disruption thesis proves right: domains and templated websites commoditise, growth fades to zero by Y5, margins compress to 31% under price competition and AI compute spend, bookings stall so the deferred-revenue tailwind shrinks, and the business exits at 12x a shrinking-share FCF.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear is raised to 25% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (Airo at a >$100M run-rate against $5.2B of revenue) and the dominant 2026 market narrative - AI-native tools disintermediating domains and website builders - is live and unresolved; customers have been flat at ~20.5M for five years, which is the bear's evidence. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right (Airo re-accelerating A&C AND Core holding ~4-5%), and management already missed on customer acquisition in early 2026. Base 50% because guidance has been met or beaten every quarter of 2026 and margins are expanding on plan.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC fully expensed and the share count held flat; forward margin built from components (NEBITDA -> SBC -> D&A -> cash tax -> capex -> working capital on the revenue change) rather than carried forward, because today's ~$1.8B FCF guide embeds a near-zero cash tax rate that expires with the DTAs and a deferred-revenue tailwind that fades with growth. The three scenarios are the three resolutions of the AI question - Airo adds (bull), offsets (base) or merely cannibalises (bear) - and the price sits between bear and base, which is the market saying it is roughly 50/50 on that question.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI-native website/presence tools or closed platforms reduce the need for a dedicated domain and templated site (the bear axis; customer count already flat since 2021)
Cash tax normalisation arrives faster than the ~4-year DTA runway modelled (e.g. a Section 382 limitation or state law change), cutting FCF ~20% sooner
Pricing power erosion across a fragmented competitor set (Wix, Squarespace, Shopify, Cloudflare, Namecheap, Big Tech) caps the margin expansion the base case assumes
Leverage: $3.8B of debt with 2027 notes ($600M) to refinance; a de-rating plus higher rates could force buyback cuts, removing the per-share tailwind the market has relied on
Terminal value is ~55% of EV in the base case; a 1pp WACC move is worth roughly $20/share
Share count: Q4-2026 buybacks are not credited; conversely the 0.94M antidilutive RSUs/PSUs included may lapse
